# Dick Moore

## Overview

- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c11 P25](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0025), [v4 c13 P6](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0006)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v4 c32 P3](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0003), [v4 c32 P6](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0006)</sub>
- **Role:** Sailor and former store clerk  <sub>[v4 c11 P25](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0025)</sub>

## Appearance

Dick was a big, handsome man with dashing ways and a high color. He had a notable eye freak, possessing one blue eye and one hazel eye, which was a Moore family trait. He also had hair that was a shade lighter than his cousin George's.

_Sources: [v4 c11 P25](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0025), [v4 c11 P27](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0027), [v4 c13 P15](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0015), [v4 c32 P12](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0012)_

## Personality

In his youth, Dick was selfish and possessive, always wanting something until he obtained it and then losing interest. He was generally agreeable when things went his way, but he possessed an ugly soul, drank heavily, and was prone to drunken brawls. After marrying Leslie, he quickly grew tired of quiet married life and sought to run off.

_Sources: [v4 c11 P25](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0025), [v4 c11 P28](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0028), [v4 c30 P44](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0044), [v4 c30 P46](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0046)_

## History

Dick Moore grew up in the Glen area, spending his summers sailing and his winters clerking in his father's store. Infatuated with Leslie West's good looks and angered by her repeated rejections, he coerced her into marriage by threatening to have his father foreclose the overdue mortgage on her family's farm. They lived together on the West place through the winter, but following Mrs. West's death the next spring, Dick grew tired of settled life and left for Nova Scotia. There, he joined his cousin George Moore on a voyage aboard the vessel *Four Sisters* bound for Havana. While in Cuba, Dick contracted yellow fever and died shortly after the ship was forced to sail without him. For thirteen years, the locals at Four Winds harbor mistook his cousin George—who suffered severe memory loss and head trauma—for Dick, believing he was alive and impaired.

_Sources: [v4 c11 P25](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0025), [v4 c11 P26](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0026), [v4 c11 P27](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0027), [v4 c11 P28](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0028), [v4 c32 P3](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0003), [v4 c32 P6](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0006), [v4 c32 P12](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0012)_
